records.title: AGROVOC concept: Plinthosols (plinthite, petroplinthite)
records.summary: Defines plinthite as iron-rich, humus-poor material that hardens irreversibly into concretions or a hardpan with repeated wetting and drying, and petroplinthite as a continuous or fractured cemented sheet. Basis for the lateritic hardpan archetype and the patchy vs continuous distinction.

records.title: Use fireplace ash sparingly to boost garden soil
records.summary: Wood ash acts like lime and adds some potassium, but 'the dose makes the poison': use sparingly, not at seeding (salts burn seedlings), never in piles, never from trash or treated wood; caustic, so protect eyes and skin. Supports the small-handful, optional-only ash guidance.

records.title: Proactive management of Striga infestation
records.summary: Striga seed persists in soil for many years; rotation or intercropping with legumes such as cowpea and groundnut, plus manure, compost and residues, reduces striga; hand pulling is labour-intensive.

records.title: Remove Striga weeds carefully from your field (radio script)
records.summary: Pull striga when flowers appear, before seed forms, without snapping the stem; bag pulled plants, take them out of the field and burn them; keep pulling every season.

records.title: Arid zone forestry, Chapter V: Special forest plantations (windbreaks and shelterbelts)
records.summary: Windbreaks and shelterbelts slow wind, cutting soil evaporation, plant water loss and wind erosion, and moderating temperature extremes. Moderately open barriers shelter a longer strip than dense ones; they should run across the prevailing wind, avoid gaps, and need upkeep. Supports the partly open dead hedge, brush windbreak and live hedge guidance.
